applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Statics and structural-analysis fundamentals from open educational sources; not a code check.

source_refs.locator: Free Body Diagrams, creating free body diagrams

claims.text: A free-body diagram defines the isolated body and the external forces, reactions, moments, dimensions, and frame needed before equilibrium equations are meaningful.

source_refs.locator: Equilibrium in Two Dimensions and Three Dimensions

claims.text: Static equilibrium requires force and moment balance for the selected body; planar problems use two force balances and one moment balance, while spatial problems require the corresponding six balances.

source_refs.locator: Free Body Diagrams, examples and two-dimensional reactions

claims.text: Changing the isolated body changes which interactions are external reactions or loads, so Fraia explanations must name the selected whole structure, member, joint, support, or cut region.

limitations: Equilibrium can reveal reaction/load inconsistencies but does not prove stability, connectivity, stiffness, or design adequacy.
This card is concept guidance and does not define numeric tolerance policy.

summary: Free-body diagrams and equilibrium equations are Fraia's first sanity-check language for explaining reactions, load paths, internal actions, and diagnostics.
